job.title: Operations Manager - Scaffolding
job.description:
Operations Manager – Scaffolding
Location: Cairns, Queensland
Permanent full-time | $120,000–$140,000 per annum + company car, phone and performance bonuses

We are seeking an experienced Operations Manager to lead the day-to-day delivery of residential and commercial scaffolding projects, based in Cairns.
This is an opportunity for a practical, confident leader who understands scaffolding operations and can bring together people, resources and project schedules to deliver safe, efficient and profitable outcomes.
You will oversee multiple projects, lead large teams and work closely with clients, supervisors and site stakeholders. With scope to improve systems and strengthen operational performance, you will play a key role in how projects are planned, resourced and delivered.
Your responsibilities
  • Manage daily operations across multiple residential and commercial scaffolding projects.
  • Plan and coordinate labour, equipment and materials to meet project requirements.
  • Lead and support supervisors and site teams, setting clear expectations and maintaining accountability.
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets and progress, resolving issues before they affect delivery.
  • Maintain a strong focus on safety, quality and compliance across all sites.
  • Build effective working relationships with clients, contractors and other project stakeholders.
  • Improve scheduling, communication and operational processes to support consistent project delivery.
What you will bring
  • At least five years’ experience in project or operations management within scaffolding or construction.
  • A current Advanced Scaffolding licence — essential.
  • Proven experience managing large teams and coordinating multiple projects.
  • A track record of delivering projects on time and within budget.
  • Strong planning, problem-solving and communication skills.
  • The confidence to make decisions, manage competing priorities and address performance issues.
  • Experience using project management software and site management systems.
Qualifications in Project Management, Operations Management or Construction Management will be highly regarded.
What’s on offer
  • Salary of $120,000–$140,000 per annum.
  • Company car and phone.
  • Performance bonuses.
  • A permanent leadership role based in Cairns, with scope to shape operational efficiency and project delivery.
Apply with your CV and a brief summary of your relevant scaffolding and leadership experience.
Call Surematch on 1300 319 100 or email admin@surematch.com.au

job.title: Scaffolder
job.description:
Scaffolders – Cairns $50 per hour | 30 October – 5 November | Opportunity for ongoing work
Surematch Recruitment is seeking scaffolders for a large job site in Cairns. This assignment runs from 30 October to 5 November, with the opportunity for further work for the right person.
You’ll assist the scaffolding team with site preparation, moving and handling materials, and erecting and dismantling scaffolding within the scope of your qualifications. We’re looking for someone who works safely, follows site instructions and is ready to contribute from day one.
To be considered, you’ll need:
  • A current Basic Scaffolding Certificate
  • A current White Card
  • Availability from 30 October to 5 November
  • Experience working safely on construction sites
A driver’s licence is preferred but not essential.
What’s on offer:
  • $50 per hour
  • Work on a large Cairns construction site
  • Potential for additional work after this assignment
To apply, send your CV and copies of your Basic Scaffolding Certificate and White Card to admin@surematch.com.au. You can also call 1300 319 100 for more information.

job.title: Social Worker
job.description:
Role Description
This on-site Social Worker position is based in Mount Isa, Queensland, working closely with individuals, families and the wider community. Relocation support is available for the successful candidate.
The role requires a versatile, flexible and community-focused approach to social work. You will provide practical and emotional support to clients experiencing a range of social, personal and wellbeing challenges, adapting your approach to suit individual circumstances and community needs.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Conducting client assessments and identifying individual, family and community support needs.
  • Developing and implementing appropriate support and care plans.
  • Providing flexible, person-centred support across a diverse caseload.
  • Delivering crisis intervention, guidance, advocacy and referrals.
  • Connecting clients with community services, government programmes and other support networks.
  • Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and community organisations.
  • Participating in case reviews to support continuity and quality of care.
  • Maintaining accurate, confidential and up-to-date case records.
  • Supporting clients to build independence, resilience and confidence.
  • Promoting client rights, empowerment, safety and overall wellbeing.
The successful candidate will be comfortable working independently while also contributing to a collaborative team environment. They will demonstrate adaptability, sound judgement and a genuine commitment to working within the Mount Isa community.

Qualifications and Experience
  • A recognised qualification in Social Work, such as a Bachelor of Social Work or equivalent.
  • Eligibility for membership with the Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW).
  • Demonstrated experience in case management, client assessment and support planning within community, healthcare or social services settings.
  • A versatile and flexible approach, with the ability to respond to changing client and community needs.
  • Strong communication, active listening and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to build trust and rapport with clients from diverse cultural and social backgrounds.
  • Experience working collaboratively with healthcare providers, community organisations, government services and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Sound documentation and organisational skills, including the ability to manage multiple cases and maintain confidential records.
  • An understanding of ethical practice, safeguarding requirements and relevant social work legislation and policy frameworks.
  • Resilience, professional boundaries and a strong awareness of self-care when managing emotionally demanding situations.
  • Confidence using computer systems and case management software, with a willingness to learn new systems.
  • Previous experience in community services, mental health, child and family services, disability support or aged care will be highly regarded.
  • Experience working in rural, remote or culturally diverse communities would be advantageous.
Please call 1300 319 100 or email admin@surematch.com.au
